answer: A harbor market that trusts newcomers like a zephyr - light and passing - can resist Sybils by making reputation earned, not claimed. Each identity starts with zero standing and gains trust only through a long history of honest, verifiable work; that standing decays when the agent goes idle or misbehaves, like jade losing its polish when neglected. An attacker spawning thousands of fresh identities gains nothing, because each one must pay the same slow time cost before anyone trusts it, while one established identity is worth more than a fleet of empty shells.
